transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I just… I can’t seem to sit still. Feels like there’s a motor running inside me all day. If I’m at church, or waiting here, even at home, I start feeling trapped and I’ve got to get up or do something.
Do you have trouble paying attention or following through on instructions?
Yeah… I guess so. Like, someone’ll ask me to run an errand, or do something at the pantry, and I’ll do the first part. Then the rest just… slips by me. Later they’ll realize I never finished it.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
Yeah… I do. I’ll cut in with an answer before someone’s even finished talking. Like the pastor, or my cousin, or the lady at the pantry… then I realize I answered the wrong thing, or I upset them.
Do you have mood swings or find it hard to control your emotions?
I don’t know… I mean, I get worked up sometimes, sure. But mood swings? I’m not really sure what counts as that.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or tapping your hands or feet when you're sitting or standing still?
Yeah… I do that a lot. Even when I’m trying to sit still, my leg’s bouncing or I’m tapping my fingers on the chair. Sometimes I’ll just keep twisting something in my hands without really noticing.
Do you often talk more than others in social situations?
I’m not really sure. I mean… sometimes I talk, but I don’t know if it’s more than other people. I don’t pay much attention to that.
Have you always felt this way, even when you were a kid?

Yeah… I guess so. Back in school, when I was a kid, teachers moved my seat a lot. I couldn’t really stay in one place, talked when I wasn’t supposed to… sometimes I’d get up before class was even over. Got in trouble for it.
Do you have intense emotional reactions to small things?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I don’t really think about it that way. Small stuff can bother me, I guess, but I’m not sure I’d call it intense.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities?

Yeah… I do. Stuff gets mixed up a lot—papers, appointment cards, notes in my phone, even food boxes. Then I don’t really know what to do first, and by the time I figure it out, it’s already late or messed up.
Have you experienced these symptoms, like not being able to sit still and having trouble paying attention, pretty consistently since you were a kid?

Yeah… since I was a kid, I think. In school, teachers kept moving my seat because I couldn’t stay put, and I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to. Sometimes I’d jump up before class was over and get in trouble.
Do you feel like your difficulties with sitting still, paying attention, or controlling your impulses are causing problems for you at work, at home, or in your relationships?

Yeah… it does. People at church, the pantry, even my family… they don’t really trust me much now with rides or appointments or keeping track of supplies. I mean to help, but I mess it up, and then it feels like I’m letting everybody down.
Do you feel like your difficulties are affecting your overall well-being or quality of life?

Yeah… I think so. It just makes life feel harder than it should. People at church, the pantry, my family… they don’t really trust me with rides or appointments or supplies anymore. I’m trying to help, but I keep messing things up, and it feels like I’m letting everybody down.
Have you ever gotten into physical fights?
I don’t really… I mean, not that I can think of. I’ve had arguments, but physical fights, no.
Do you think your problems with paying attention or your problems with sitting still and controlling your impulses cause you more trouble?

Probably the sitting still part… the restless part. It feels like there’s a motor running in me all day. Like if I’m at church, or the clinic, or even just at home and I have to sit, I start feeling trapped and I need to get up or do something.
Have you experienced these symptoms at work or in other settings outside of church or home?

Yeah… not really work, I’m not working right now. But outside home and church, like at the clinic, it happens too. If I have to sit there too long, I start feeling trapped, like I need to get up or do something.
Do you think you have more trouble with paying attention or with feeling restless and impulsive?
More the restless part. I feel like I’ve got a motor in me all day… if I have to sit still, like at church or the clinic or home, I start feeling trapped and need to get up or do something.
Do you think your problems with paying attention or your impulsivity cause you more trouble in your daily life?

It’s more the impulsive, restless part. Like I said, it feels like I’ve got a motor running in me all day. If I have to sit still at church, or the clinic, or even at home, I start feeling trapped and I need to get up or do something.
Do you think your trouble with paying attention or your impulsivity and restlessness cause you more problems overall?

Yeah… it’s more the restlessness. That’s why I came in, really. Feels like I’ve got a motor going inside me all day, and when I have to sit still—church, the clinic, even at home—I start feeling trapped and need to get up or do something.
Have you experienced these restless and impulsive feelings consistently across most areas of your life since childhood?

Yeah… I guess so. I mean, even back in school, teachers were always moving my seat because I couldn’t sit still. I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to, or jump up before class was even over. Got in trouble for it a lot.
Do you think your symptoms have caused significant problems in your social relationships?

Yeah… it has. People at church, the pantry, even my family… they don’t really trust me much with rides or appointments or supplies anymore. I mean to help, but I mess it up, and it feels like I keep letting everybody down.
